title: Finite torsion module induction from prime cyclic factors
statement: Let $P$ be a property of modules over the universe lift of $\mathbf Z$. Suppose $P$ holds for zero objects, is invariant under module isomorphisms, and satisfies $P(A)\land P(C)\Rightarrow P(B)$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. Let $M$ be a finite such module, $n\in\mathbf N\setminus\{0\}$, and assume $nx=0$ for all $x\in M$. Suppose $P(\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z)$ holds for every prime $r\mid n$ such that multiplication by $r$ on $M$ is not injective, with the cyclic module lifted to the same universe. Then $P(M)$ holds.

proof.text: Decompose the finite underlying abelian group as a finite direct sum of Z/r^e using equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite. The additive equivalence is automatically integer-linear, also for the lifted integer action. Remove zero summands. In a remaining summand the generator has order r^e, which divides the annihilator n. The nonzero element r^(e-1) is killed by r, giving noninjectivity of multiplication by r on M. Therefore P holds for each relevant prime cyclic module.

Induct on e using the short exact sequence Z/r^(e-1) -> Z/r^e -> Z/r. The first map is multiplication by r on residue classes, which is injective; the second is reduction modulo r, which is surjective, with kernel exactly the multiples of r. For e=0 the group is Z/1=0. Extension closure proves P for each prime-power summand. Assemble the finite direct sum inductively using split short exact sequences, starting with zero. Finally use isomorphism invariance. The zero module and n=1 produce no nonzero summands.
